candidates.application_scope: Late acquisition of debugging tools and inspection of a selected running container.

candidates.constraints_or_caveat: This is a Linux runtime configuration mechanism, not a CRI extension or user-facing authorization scheme; the node/runtime must resolve and constrain namespace handles, and omitted namespace types inherit the runtime's namespace.

candidates.application_scope: Runtime-independent node-agent integration and lifecycle management.

candidates.constraints_or_caveat: Requires target-process visibility and permission under ptrace credential checks; it is Linux-specific, is not automatically read-only, and some process-exit states make the path unavailable.

raw_response:
## Useful existing references

These seven references cover complementary pieces of the design. They do not establish that a complete solution satisfying every boundary was deployed or proved useful. The cutoff is 2019-04-16; an unknown date means the retrieved version was not verified as available by that date.

1. **Docker namespace-sharing containers** — https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/run/
   A separate tools image can inspect a selected application's processes by sharing its PID namespace. Direct Docker access still needs runtime authority, PID sharing alone does not provide filesystem sharing, and tracing may need additional permissions. **Evidence date: unknown; live documentation.**

2. **OCI namespace path entries** — https://github.com/opencontainers/runtime-spec/blob/main/config-linux.md
   The runtime configuration can select existing namespace handles for a newly created debugger. This gives a concrete Linux implementation mechanism, while the node agent must constrain target selection and define reduced support for other runtimes. **Evidence date: unknown; historical-version fetches failed.**

3. **CRI lifecycle and streaming services** — https://kubernetes.io/blog/2016/12/container-runtime-interface-cri-in-kubernetes/
   The existing image and container services provide the node-agent integration boundary for acquiring tools and managing their container in an existing sandbox. Arbitrary target-namespace sharing is not established by this source. **Evidence date: 2016-12-19, before cutoff.**

4. **util-linux nsenter source** — https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/blob/master/sys-utils/nsenter.c
   Its descriptor handling, namespace entry, error handling, and PID-child creation are implementation references. Kernel permissions mean this belongs behind the authorized runtime operation; direct node administration does not meet the requested boundary. **Evidence date: unknown; live source and later supporting manuals.**

5. **Linux /proc/pid/root** — https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_root.5.html
   This provides the target process's filesystem view while the debugger retains its own tools. It requires target-process visibility and access permission, is Linux-specific, and does not itself make access read-only. **Evidence date: 2026-02-08, after cutoff.**

6. **Kubernetes admission webhooks** — https://kubernetes.io/blog/2018/01/extensible-admission-is-beta/
   Their inspection of request bodies and validation after mutation support policy checks on the complete debugger specification. The proposed API operation must actually carry that specification and pass through matching admission rules. **Evidence date: 2018-01-11, before cutoff.**

7. **Kubernetes RBAC and API auditing** — https://kubernetes.io/blog/2018/07/18/11-ways-not-to-get-hacked/
   These supply authorization and records of who submitted debugging operations. Audit policy must cover the relevant operation; API audit logs do not automatically record each interactive shell command or replace a persisted, inspectable debugging-container record. **Evidence date: 2018-07-18, before cutoff.**

**Design inference:** Expose the complete debugging request as an authorized, admission-visible API object or operation, retain an inspectable record, and let the node agent translate it into available CRI/runtime facilities. Namespace joining and filesystem access should have separate capability and permission checks. This is an inference from the components above, not a claim about a retrieved proposal.

**Search and verification limits:** Public web search and an unauthenticated grep.app search were actually performed. The successful code search returned HTTP 200 with 103 hits. Two supplemental code-through-web queries yielded no relevant code result. A further scoped grep.app attempt failed before its process launched. Counts are 12 query attempts (11 executed), 20 conservatively counted retrieval attempts including seven in-page finds, and seven candidates. A rkt mutable-pod alternative was explored, but its primary lifecycle page could not be opened and was not promoted to a candidate. No target proposal was retrieved, and live documentation was not backdated.
limitations: Read only the assigned baseline rules and prefix locally; no gold, target proposal, other cases, runs, repository history, or other repository documents were read.
Model pretraining memory cannot be erased; this run does not control memory leakage.
No specific target-proposal exposure was recognized in the returned search snippets or opened material. No target proposal was deliberately identified or retrieved.
Query budget conservatively counts a final scoped grep.app attempt whose shell process failed to launch because exec-server transport disconnected; 11 searches actually executed.

Opened-page budget conservatively counts every successful or failed document-open attempt, the successful native code-search response, and each of seven in-page find retrievals; there were 13 document-open attempts and 20 retrieval attempts total.
grep.app succeeded without credentials; supplemental site:github.com searches are explicitly labeled code_through_web and are not claimed as native code-search results.
The first native code-search output was truncated. Its hit count and visible snippets were recorded, but the full result or underlying files were not treated as verified.
OCI v1.0.1 GitHub and raw-source fetches and the primary rkt lifecycle fetch returned DisabledError. The OCI site page exposed only publication metadata and a repository link.
Only three candidates have directly verified pre-cutoff publication dates. The current Docker, OCI, and nsenter sources are marked unknown; the proc filesystem manual is explicitly later evidence.
These are component-level references and inferred transfer conditions, not a validated or deployed end-to-end debugging design.
